title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, and experimental validation reveal that TPM1 suppresses M2 macrophage polarization and enhances chemosensitivity in acute myeloid leukemia.
summary: ML feature selection across AML transcriptomic/proteomic datasets prioritized TPM1; cell-line perturbations and a xenograft model then showed TPM1-linked AML growth, Ara-C sensitivity, and M2 macrophage effects. MeRIP/RIP, reporter, and mRNA-stability assays support an FTO/m6A mechanism destabilizing TPM1. This is preclinical evidence, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: LASSO, SVM-RFE and random-forest analyses of AML transcriptomic/proteomic datasets selected TPM1 as a candidate, which was then experimentally perturbed.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: TPM1 overexpression reduced AML cell growth, increased apoptosis/oxidative stress and Ara-C sensitivity, and attenuated M2 polarization; mechanistic assays support FTO-dependent m6A-mediated TPM1 mRNA destabilization.
evidence.unknown: Follow-up includes AML cell-line perturbations, macrophage co-culture, MeRIP/RIP and mRNA-stability assays, and xenograft groups of six mice; evidence remains preclinical.
evidence.ai_role: LASSO, SVM-RFE and random-forest analyses of AML transcriptomic/proteomic datasets selected TPM1 as a candidate, which was then experimentally perturbed.
